newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle seen up $1 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle seen up $1 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle prices next week were seen up at least $1.00 per cwt at $66.00 following a bullishly-construed USDA monthly Cattle on Feed Report on Friday, feedlot sources said.

In feedlots with capacity of 1,000 head or more in the seven key states, USDA pegged December placements at 98 percent of a year ago, well below the average trade estimate of 108.2 percent and range of 103.0-112.0 percent. December marketings were put at 100.0 percent of a year ago, which was below the average of 101.8 percent and near the low end of the range of 99.0-107.1. Cattle on feed were pegged at 103 percent versus the estimate of 104.2.
The bulk of this week's cattle sold at $65.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from a week ago, with a few loads trading Friday at $64.50 to $65.00.
Several feedlot operators said late Friday they were going to raise asking prices to $68.00 on Monday because of the light government placements figure.
"Sixty-six dollar (trades) are a given," a Texas source said.

Without the pressure from perceived heavy supplies behind them, feedlot managers said they could slow marketings down from the current pace that has many cattle being sold up to four weeks ahead of schedule.
"I had been trying to push them through quickly at any price, but now I'm going to slow down and feed those 90-day cattle up to weight," a Kansas feedlot manager said.

Average weights of slaughter cattle this week continued to be well below last year. USDA estimated cattle weights this week at 1,162 lbs, above 1,154 lbs estimated last week but well below 1,188 lbs in the same week last year.
